# Navidrome — BowPlayer fork

[Navidrome](https://github.com/navidrome/navidrome) with two additions: **canvases**, short looping videos for songs, the way Spotify shows them, and **Connect**, a relay that lets one account's players see and control each other, like Spotify Connect. Everything else is upstream Navidrome, unchanged; for Navidrome itself see the [upstream README](../README.md) and [navidrome.org](https://www.navidrome.org).

## Canvases

A canvas is an `.mp4` kept next to the music. Navidrome's scanner ignores it.

| File | Plays for |
|---|---|
| `<song file name without extension>.canvas.mp4` | that song |
| `canvas.mp4` | every song in that folder (an album or a disc) without its own |

For example `Disc 1/1.01 - Full Moon Full Life.flac` gets `Disc 1/1.01 - Full Moon Full Life.canvas.mp4`. Short (3–8 s), portrait 9:16, H.264 without audio works everywhere.

### API

- `GET /rest/getCanvas?id=<song id>` with the usual Subsonic authentication serves the song's canvas (`video/mp4`, with Range support), or answers **404** when it has none.
- `getOpenSubsonicExtensions` lists **`bowCanvas`** (version 1), so clients ask for canvases only on servers that have them.

Any Subsonic client keeps working; ones that don't know the extension never see it.

## Connect

A user's players keep an event stream open and the server relays between them: which devices are online, the state of the one that plays, and commands sent to it. Signing in works like any Subsonic call, so a player only sees the same account's devices. Nothing is stored: the active device and its last state live in memory until the server restarts. The protocol is `protocol/connect.md` in the BowPlayer repo.

- `GET /rest/connect?device=<id>&name=<name>&platform=<desktop|android|web>`: a `text/event-stream` of `hello`, `devices`, `state`, `command` and `ping` events, open while the device is online.
- `POST /rest/connectState?device=<id>[&claim=true]` with a JSON body: the device's state (the queue only when it changed; the server keeps the last one). A playing or claiming device becomes the active one, and the one it replaces gets a `pause` command.
- `POST /rest/connectCommand?device=<id>&target=<id>` with a JSON body (`{"cmd": …}`): a command for another device; error 70 when it's offline.
- `getOpenSubsonicExtensions` lists **`bowConnect`** (version 1).

A reverse proxy in front of the server must not buffer the event stream (the response carries `X-Accel-Buffering: no` for nginx).

## What differs from upstream

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `server/subsonic/canvas.go`, `canvas_test.go` | the endpoint and its tests |
| `server/subsonic/connect.go`, `connect_test.go` | the Connect relay and its tests |
| `server/subsonic/api.go` | the routes |
| `server/subsonic/opensubsonic.go`, `opensubsonic_test.go` | the `bowCanvas` and `bowConnect` extensions |
| `.github/workflows/bow-image.yml` | builds the Docker image |
| `.github/README.md` | this file |
| `deploy/compose.yml` | a Portainer / Compose stack |

The `bow` branch is an upstream release tag plus these commits. Updating is a rebase onto the next tag.

## Docker image

Each push to `bow` builds upstream's Dockerfile, unchanged, for `linux/amd64` and pushes:

- `ghcr.io/ibowie/navidrome:bow`: the latest build
- `ghcr.io/ibowie/navidrome:<upstream tag>-bow.<n>`: a pinned build to roll back to

[`deploy/compose.yml`](../deploy/compose.yml) is a drop-in for a stock Navidrome stack: only the image changes. Going back to stock Navidrome is changing the image back.
